title: Coinduced total Hom complexes and K-injective targets
statement:
Let $P\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings. Work with unbounded cochain complexes, the product total Hom complex of [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex], and K-injectivity of [def-pur-kinjective-complex] on the one-object identity-cover ringed site. Let $U$ be termwise restriction of scalars. For any $P$-complex $I$, set $J(I)=\operatorname{Hom}_P^\bullet(A[0],I)$, with $(a h)(b)=h(ba)$ and differential induced by $I$. For every $A$-complex $E$ there is a natural isomorphism of $P$-complexes
$$T_{E,I}:U\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(E,J(I))\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_P^\bullet(UE,I),\qquad T(f)(x)=f(x)(1),$$
whose inverse on homogeneous cochains of every integer degree is $S(g)(x)(a)=g(ax)$. These maps commute with the Hom differential $d(f)=d_I f-(-1)^{\deg f}f d_E$, are natural under precomposition in $E$ and postcomposition in $I$, and carry chain homotopies to chain homotopies. If $I$ is K-injective over $P$, then $J(I)$ is K-injective over $A$. For a K-injective $I$ representing $Y\in D(P)$, its restricted complex $UJ(I)$ represents $R\operatorname{Hom}_P(A[0],Y)$ of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], with the displayed $A$-action on $J(I)$. No boundedness, flatness, finiteness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tags 0A70 (lemma-right-adjoint) and 0A71 (lemma-RHom-ext): K-injective coinduction model; explicit total-Hom transposition and null-homotopy argument expanded from these, with derived.tex Tag 070H (definition-K-injective).

proof.text: By [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex], since $A[0]$ has just one nonzero term, $J(I)^q=\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,I^q)$ and $d_J(h)=d_I\circ h$. The formula $(a h)(b)=h(ba)$ gives an $A$-module: $(a(ch))(b)=h((ba)c)=((ac)h)(b)$ and $1h=h$, and distributivity follows from additivity. The $P$-action agrees with restriction since $h(b\varphi(p))=p h(b)$, where $\varphi:P\to A$. Also $d_J(ah)(b)=d_I(h(ba))=(a d_Jh)(b)$ and $d_J^2h=d_I^2h=0$. Thus this is an $A$-complex.

source.place: Tags 0A70 (lemma-right-adjoint), 0A71 (lemma-RHom-ext): the coinduced complex; action and differential expanded.

proof.text: For each integer $n$, define $T^n(f)^p(x)=f^p(x)(1)$ and $S^n(g)^p(x)(a)=g^p(ax)$ on the product factors of [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex]. These formulas are additive and $P$-linear. For $S$, the inner map is $P$-linear since $g^p(\varphi(p)ax)=p g^p(ax)$, and the outer map is $A$-linear since $g^p(acx)=(c S^n(g)^p(x))(a)$. Evaluation gives $T^nS^n(g)(x)=g(x)$ and $S^nT^n(f)(x)(a)=f(ax)(1)=(a f(x))(1)=f(x)(a)$. Hence $T^n,S^n$ are inverse $P$-linear maps for every $n$; the products over all $p$ impose no finite-support condition.

source.place: Tags 0A70 and 0A71: explicit homogeneous transposition formulas.

proof.text: Use the differential of [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex]. For $x\in E^p$ and homogeneous $f$ of degree $n$, $T^{n+1}(df)^p(x)=d_I(f^p(x)(1))-(-1)^n f^{p+1}(d_E x)(1)=(dT^n(f))^p(x)$. Conversely, $(dS^n(g))^p(x)(a)=d_I(g^p(ax))-(-1)^n g^{p+1}(a d_E x)=S^{n+1}(dg)^p(x)(a)$ because $d_E(ax)=a d_Ex$. Thus the inverse maps are chain maps with exactly the asserted sign, for negative as well as positive $n$.

source.place: Tags 0A70 and 0A71: total-Hom transposition, differential calculation expanded.

proof.text: For chain maps $\alpha:E\to E_1$ and $\beta:I\to I_1$, define $J(\beta)(h)=\beta\circ h$; it is $A$-linear and commutes with the differentials. If $f$ has source $E_1$, evaluating on $x\in E$ gives $T_{E,I_1}(J(\beta)\circ f\circ\alpha)(x)=\beta(f(\alpha x)(1))=(\beta\circ T_{E_1,I}(f)\circ U\alpha)(x)$. The inverse identity follows either by applying the inverse $S$, or directly from $\alpha(ax)=a\alpha(x)$. These are the precomposition and postcomposition naturality identities in every degree of the product total Hom [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex].

source.place: Tag 0A70 (lemma-right-adjoint): naturality of the displayed transposition, expanded.

proof.text: By [def-pur-kinjective-complex], a homotopy between chain maps $f,f_1:E\to J(I)$ is a degree $-1$ cochain $h$ with $f-f_1=d_Jh+h d_E$. The differential calculation gives $T(f)-T(f_1)=d_I T(h)+T(h)d_E$, so $T(h)$ is the transposed homotopy; the identical calculation with $S$ gives the converse. A homotopy $k$ between maps $I\to I_1$ is also carried by $J$ to $J(k)^q(h)=k^q\circ h$: postcomposing $\beta-\beta_1=d k+k d$ with $h$ gives $J(\beta)-J(\beta_1)=d J(k)+J(k)d$.

source.place: Tag 070H (definition-K-injective), with the transposition of Tags 0A70 and 0A71; explicit homotopy equations.

proof.text: Let $N$ be an acyclic $A$-complex. Restriction $U$ leaves the underlying groups and differentials unchanged, so its kernels, images, and their quotient are unchanged as groups: $H^q(UN)=U H^q(N)=0$ for every $q$. This uses precisely $H^q=\ker d^q/\operatorname{im}d^{q-1}$ from [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; in particular $UN$ is acyclic without any flatness assumption.

source.place: Tag 0A70 (lemma-right-adjoint): exactness of restriction; kernel/image argument expanded.

proof.text: Assume $I$ is K-injective and let $f:N\to J(I)$ be a chain map with $N$ acyclic. The preceding acyclicity argument and [def-pur-kinjective-complex] give a $P$-linear homotopy $k$ with $T(f)=d_I k+k d_N$. Set $h=S^{(-1)}(k)$, where the superscript $(-1)$ denotes the cochain degree (so $h^p(x)(a)=k^p(ax)$). The differential identity for $S$ gives $d_J h+h d_N=S^0(T(f))=f$. This $h$ is $A$-linear by the formula already checked. Every map from an acyclic complex is therefore null-homotopic, which is exactly K-injectivity of $J(I)$.

source.place: Tag 070H (definition-K-injective), applied to the adjunction of Tag 0A70; null-homotopy argument expanded.

proof.text: Let I be K-injective and QI isomorphic to Y. First identify UJ(I) with moduleHomComplex(A[0],I) by evaluation at the degree-zero source factor, with inverse insertion into that factor. Compare this total Hom complex with the existing monoidal internalHomObj(A[0],I) by its product projections. The differentials agree: the source differential vanishes and its nonzero source factor is p=0, where the signed comparison is the identity. The right-derived internal-Hom unit is invertible on I, by the K-injective derivability structure used to construct [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Uniqueness of right adjoints compares that right-derived functor with ihom(Q(A[0])). Compose these isomorphisms and transport the second variable along QI ≅ Y. This proves the desired arbitrary-representative clause for the recorded ordinaryModuleDerivedInternalHom abbreviation. No boundedness, flatness, finiteness or Noetherian hypothesis enters.

source.place: Tag 0A71 (lemma-RHom-ext), proof: choose a K-injective representative; also sites-cohomology.tex Tag 08J7 (section-internal-hom).
